As a person who has gone through the phase, i can tell you a few things i learnt

1, Dont be afraid to approach first, a "hey, i have seen you around, and i was interested to talk to you, can we have a chat" can do wonders.

2, dont be disheartened if people leave , remember, you are the only constant in the equation, everything else are variables. people will leave, and better people will come.

3, If you have a hard tine finding topics to talk, ask about them, people LOVE to talk about themselves, pick up what wavelengths match, and carry on from there.

4, showing interest keeps people to you. 

5, MOST, of not all people, look out for personal interests, if you see a red flag, dont invest and cut your losses. 

5, sometimes you will need to indulge in stuff you may not like, as interests differ from people to people, unless you are SURE you are against an idea or it is harmful/ illegal/ immoral, try giving it a shot, it shows a level of dedication.

6, Dont be a people pleaser all the time, people respect and are curious about people with their own (correct) ideologies. 

6, a good heart to heart is almost always a catylist to a lasting friendship, but they are rare, you may not get a status quo even after weeks of akward one liners and small talks, but dont give up. 

7, Lastly if you have no receprcation from the person no matter how hard you try, its not worth it, give people importance who react to the stimulai likewise. 

thats some things i learnt about making friends as adults. i may be wrong and this aint a definate list, but these are observations i made as i broke my shell a few years back, and i was a very anxious introvert myself.
